what_it_does: Before a chip ships, engineers run Automatic Test Pattern Generation (ATPG) — a process that figures out which patterns of input signals will expose hidden manufacturing defects. Traditional ATPG tools based on a logic-puzzle-solving technique called SAT (satisfiability solving) are thorough but slow, because they force every input wire to have a definite value even when many don't matter for detecting a given defect; this inflates the number of test patterns needed. PastATPG adapts the SAT solver to allow partial answers — leaving irrelevant inputs unspecified — which produces fewer, denser test patterns and runs faster. The paper pairs this modified solver with smarter search rules tuned to circuit structure, and integrates it into a hybrid framework alongside traditional structural test methods.
